transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been going on that brought you here today?

Well... I suppose I've just been getting stuck doing these little routines lately. Um. It's just things like... washing my hands again after I handle my wrist brace. Or rechecking the stove and the front door. 

Sometimes I end up silently counting through steps before I leave the house. It's... well, it's starting to make me late for things. Even when I know I've already done enough. That's mainly it.
Do you feel anxious or upset if you aren't able to complete these routines the way you want to?

I suppose you could say that. I wouldn't call it being upset, exactly. Just... bothered. 

Like I said, if I don't finish checking the door, or washing up after I touch this brace... it just nags at me. Even though I know perfectly well I've already done enough. It's just easier to finish the routine so I can move on, even if it ends up making me late.
Do you ever have thoughts or images come into your mind that you don't want there, that bother or upset you?

Well... yes, I suppose so. 

Sometimes I’ll just be sitting at home reading, or... getting ready for my shift at the museum. And this, well, this ugly little thought just sort of barges in. Just telling me that I’ve left something unsafe, or touched something unclean. Or that I’ve somehow put someone at risk. 

I know perfectly well it’s out of proportion, of course. But... yes. They do come to mind.
When you have those thoughts about something being unsafe or unclean, do you feel like you have to do something specific, like checking or washing, to make sure nothing bad happens or to feel better?

Yes... I suppose that's exactly it. 

Like I mentioned before, that's why I end up doing those little routines. The washing, or going back to check the stove. If I just do it, or count through my steps... it settles the thought. It's just easier to do it and be done with it, even if it ends up making me late.
